**Geographic focus:**
Global — primary focus on US, with secondary focus on Europe, Japan

**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical report [YES] — recaps recent data, moves, and Fed commentary
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — NFP Friday, CPI Sep 11, Fed rate decision this month, Waller speech
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — Broadcom AI chip sales 2-year outlook; BOJ policy trajectory; sustained inflation pressures

**Synopsis:**
Bond markets stabilised slightly after recent volatility, with US and JGB yields edging lower. Oil above $90 on US-Iran escalation is sustaining inflation pressure. Fed rate hike odds for the current month jumped to 67% (from 37% a week prior), though NY Fed's Williams pushed back mildly. Upcoming NFP (Friday) and CPI (Sep 11) are the key data triggers. BOJ rate hike prospects are building on strong services data, supporting the yen. Equity futures pointed to minor gains in both Europe and the US.

---

**Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?**
Relevance: YES — the article is heavily centred on Fed rate expectations, US bond yields, labour data, CPI, oil-driven inflation, and US equity futures.

**Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?**
Relevance: 85
Probability of increase: 67% (per CME FedWatch as cited in the article)

**Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?**
Relevance: 30
Probability of holding: 33% (implied residual from the 67% hike probability cited)

**Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?**
Relevance: 0

**Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?**
Sentiment: +55 — The dominant signal is hawkish: hike probability nearly doubled in a week to 67%, oil above $90 is stoking inflation fears, and the next speaker (Waller) has previously advocated for higher rates. Williams' mild pushback for more data provides a modest dovish offset, but the net tone is meaningfully more hawkish than prior.
